extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, picture editors, news organizations, and prospective entrants to the Pulitzer Prize (Feature Photography) category
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for entries to the Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography: what kinds of photographs (single image or series) and qualities (news relevance, depth, emotional impact, storytelling, etc.) the prize seeks. Useful for photographers and editors preparing submissions or assessing work against the category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished example of feature photography
rubrics_metrics.description: For a distinguished example of feature photography, which may be a single photograph or series of photographs of general news that may be taken over time and that illuminate a subject in great depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the category definition on the Pulitzer site; it states the core requirement: work must be a 'distinguished example' of feature photography, addressing general news and illuminating a subject 'in great depth.' The prize amount (Fifteen thousand dollars) is also noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable formats — single photograph or series
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries 'may be a single photograph or series of photographs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The category explicitly allows either a single image or a multi-image essay/series as an entry; selection examples include both single powerful images and extended photo essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: News relevance / subject: general news
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature Photography entries should be of 'general news'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners and finalists are grounded in newsworthy subjects (e.g., migrants, pandemics, conflict, public-health crises), demonstrating that the category prizes photojournalistic coverage tied to current events and issues of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of treatment / illumination of subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should 'illuminate a subject in great depth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges reward sustained, probing treatment of a subject — long-form projects and intimate essays that reveal layers of context and meaning (examples: longitudinal photo essays of families, prisons, refugee journeys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal scope / longitudinal reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs 'may be taken over time', permitting submissions that document change or sustained observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries that track subjects across days, months, or years (longitudinal storytelling) fit the category; many winners are multi-session projects showing development or decline over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional resonance and intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Work often conveys strong emotional impact — described across winners as 'heart‑wrenching', 'achingly beautiful', 'poignant', 'intimate'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The category favors images that create empathy and emotional connection (intimate portraits, candid moments of vulnerability) that help viewers grasp human consequences of larger issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative / photo-essay storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective entries tell a story or form a cohesive essay — winners are called 'photo essay', 'chronicle', 'portrayal', or 'story'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for coherent narrative flow or thematic unity across images (sequence, pacing, selection) that together deepen understanding of the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of aesthetic quality and documentary weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Many winning entries combine aesthetic/visual strength ('beautiful', 'brilliant', 'memorable') with documentary seriousness ('devastation', 'horror', 'violence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs that are both visually compelling and journalistically rigorous — where composition, light, and form serve to deepen the reportage — are rewarded (examples note 'beauty and composure intertwined with devastation').

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure of injustice, violence, or urgent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries frequently expose or document human-rights abuses, violence, suffering, or systemic problems ('exposed the world to the violence Rohingya refugees faced', 'capture the traumatic legacy of Assad’s torture chambers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that brings hidden or underreported abuses and crises to public attention — prompting viewers to confront uncomfortable realities — aligns with the category's values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of place and contextual grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs that offer a 'heightened sense of place' and contextualize subjects within their environments are highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should orient viewers geographically and socially, helping them understand setting, conditions, and the broader context surrounding individual subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage and difficulty of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges have cited 'gripping, courageous photographs' and images made under difficult conditions (e.g., communications blackout, conflict zones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work produced at personal risk, in restrictive or dangerous environments, or under challenging logistical conditions is recognized — especially when risk yields reporting that would otherwise be inaccessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassion and ethical portrayal of subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners' descriptions emphasize compassionate chronicling and sensitive portrayal of vulnerable people ('compassionate chronicle', 'sensitive photo essay').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical, respectful treatment of subjects — showing dignity, avoiding exploitation — is an implicit criterion in awarding feature photography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesiveness and editorial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning portfolios are described as 'cohesive' or 'a portfolio' that together create a strong, unified presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and entrants should assemble images into a coherent package where sequencing and selection enhance the overall impact rather than being a loose collection of singles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and excellence across varied subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Some awards note 'consistently excellent work on a variety of subjects.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For staff or multi-topic portfolios, sustained high quality across different assignments or subjects can be a positive factor.
